transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I'm here because... well, it's my eating. What scares me is that once I start eating, especially when I’m alone in the kitchen... Which is a lovely kitchen, we actually just put in new cabinets last spring. Hickory wood. My husband didn't want to spend the money, but I told him, if I'm going to be in there all the time, I want it to look nice. He's always so cheap about house stuff, but then he'll go buy a new set of golf clubs without blinking an eye. It drives me completely crazy. 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. When I'm alone in there and I start eating, it feels like I’ve just stepped aside. I can’t make myself stop, even though I’m telling myself the whole time, ‘Janet, put it away.’ I just keep going. It's so frustrating. Kind of like trying to get the neighborhood association to fix the potholes on our street, honestly. I swear, I've called them three times this week and it just goes straight to voicemail. But yes, the eating is why I made the appointment.
How do you feel after one of these eating episodes when you can't stop?

Oh, I feel just awful. I mean, I just sit there afterward and think, 'Janet, you are forty-eight years old, you are way too old to be acting like this.' And the guilt is terrible, especially because a lot of times I've eaten food I meant to share with other people. 

Like last Tuesday, I bought these beautiful bakery cookies for my book club. We were reading that new historical fiction book... oh, what was it called? The one with the clock on the cover. The author was actually on one of the morning shows recently, wearing the most gorgeous silk scarf. I love silk scarves, but they always slip right off my shoulders, I just don't have the posture for them. My sister Carol wears them beautifully, but she does pilates, so she has that perfect posture. She's always trying to get me to go to a class with her, but it's all the way across town and the traffic on Route 9 is a nightmare in the mornings. 

But anyway, I ended up eating the entire box of those cookies before the ladies even arrived. I just sat there at the kitchen island feeling so ashamed of myself, looking at the empty box and realizing I'd wasted all that food. I always swear up and down and promise myself it won't ever happen again, but... well, it does.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after one of these eating episodes?

No, no, I've never done that. I couldn't. Just the thought of throwing up makes my stomach turn. I mean, I hate being sick. When I had the stomach flu last winter—oh, it was right around Christmas, which was just a disaster because I was supposed to host the family dinner. We always do a big honey-baked ham, and my mother-in-law makes her scalloped potatoes. Well, she calls them scalloped, but honestly, they're just sliced potatoes swimming in heavy cream. I don't know how her cholesterol isn't through the roof. My doctor told me to watch my dairy intake, actually, which is why I switched to almond milk for my coffee. But then I read an article saying almond milk is terrible for the environment because it takes so much water to grow the almonds, especially in California. And with the droughts they've been having out there, it just feels so irresponsible, you know? So I tried oat milk, but it just doesn't taste the same. But anyway, no, I don't make myself sick or anything like that. I just sit there feeling terrible about what I've done.
Do you feel like you're in control of your eating during these episodes?

Well, no, not at all. That's actually the scariest part for me. Like I was saying before, once I start, especially when I'm alone in that kitchen... it's like I've just stepped aside. I'm completely out of the driver's seat. I'll be standing there, eating, and my brain is screaming, 'Janet, put it away! Stop it!' but my hands just keep going. It's like my body is doing one thing and my mind is just trapped watching it happen. 

It reminds me of when my husband was teaching our son, Mark, how to drive. Mark is twenty-two now, graduated from Penn State last spring—we were so proud, though the commencement speaker was terribly boring, just droned on and on about the global economy. I think half the stadium fell asleep. But anyway, when Mark was sixteen and learning to drive, he accidentally hit the gas instead of the brake in an empty parking lot, and my husband said it was the most helpless feeling in the world, just watching the car go and not being able to stop it. That's exactly how my eating feels. I just can't make myself stop.
How often do these episodes of eating uncontrollably happen to you?

Well, if I look back at my kitchen calendar... I keep a big floral calendar right on the fridge to keep track of everything. It's one of those Thomas Kinkade ones, with the little cottages and the glowing windows. My aunt Susan used to collect his paintings, actually. Her whole living room looked like a little village, which was a bit much, if you ask me, but it made her happy. She lived in this beautiful old Victorian house in Connecticut, and every fall the leaves in her yard would turn the most vibrant colors. I always meant to go visit her more often during autumn, but the drive up I-95 is just dreadful, especially with all the construction they've been doing near New Haven. I swear that highway has been under construction since the nineties. 

But anyway, looking at my calendar, and the weeks I've been going to volunteer at the food bank... which I really do love doing, sorting the cans is so relaxing, though some people donate the strangest things. Last week someone dropped off four jars of pickled beets that expired in 2018! I mean, who keeps pickled beets that long? 

But looking back, these episodes... they've been happening most weeks. Usually once or twice a week, I'd say. And it's been going on like this for many months now, just over and over.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?

Weight? You know, I haven't really checked. I don't keep a scale in the bathroom anymore. I used to have one of those fancy digital ones, but the battery died and it took those little flat, round ones—I think they're called CR2032s? I can never find them at CVS. They always have the AAAs and the hearing aid batteries, but never the ones I actually need. It's exactly like when you go looking for a specific greeting card and all they have left are the ones with terrible jokes. 

I was trying to find a retirement card for my neighbor, Bill, just last week. He was a postal worker for thirty years, such a lovely man, he always made sure our packages didn't get wet on the porch when it rained. He's moving down to Florida now, somewhere near Sarasota, I think. My sister went to Sarasota for a timeshare presentation a few years ago and said the humidity was just absolutely relentless. It ruined her hair for the entire trip, and she spends a fortune at the salon getting these keratin treatments. 

But anyway... what were we saying? Oh, right, my weight. No, I haven't really noticed any big changes. My clothes seem to fit about the same, I suppose.
Do you worry about gaining weight?

Worry about gaining weight? Um, not really, no. I mean, I don't sit around stressing about it like my friend Brenda does. Oh my goodness, Brenda is always on some new diet. Right now she is doing that one where you only eat meat and cheese, keto I think it is called? It sounds absolutely exhausting. 

We went to lunch at Panera last Tuesday, and you know how they give you that nice piece of French baguette with your soup? Well, she wouldn't even touch it. She made them swap it for an apple, and then she didn't even eat the apple because she said it had too much sugar! It just seems like a miserable way to live. And speaking of apples, we went apple picking at this orchard up in Bucks County a few years ago, and the bees were just horrendous. I got stung right on the ankle and it swelled up to the size of a grapefruit. I had to wear my husband's slippers for three days because none of my shoes would fit. My husband has these big fleece-lined moccasins, they are so warm, but they looked absolutely ridiculous on me. I couldn't even walk down the stairs without tripping. 

But, um... what was the question? Oh, worrying about weight. No, I don't really worry about gaining it. It is really just the eating itself that bothers me, not so much what it does to my waistline.
Do you have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, and then feel guilty or ashamed afterwards?

Yes... yes, I do. It's usually with food I actually bought for something else, too. Like last week, I bought all these nice bakery cookies for my book club. We meet on Thursdays, usually at Linda's house. Linda has this gorgeous sunroom with white wicker furniture that she got at an estate sale. I just love estate sales, you can find the most incredible vintage Pyrex bowls if you get there early enough on a Saturday morning. I collect the pink gooseberry pattern, actually. It's so hard to find the big mixing bowls with the paint still intact because people just put them right in the dishwasher, which completely ruins the finish. My mother had a beautiful set that she ruined that exact way in the eighties when we first got a dishwasher. It was one of those loud portable ones with the butcher block top that you had to wheel over and hook up to the kitchen sink faucet... 

But anyway, I bought those cookies for the book club, and before I even made it to Thursday, I just sat down at my kitchen island and ate... all of them. Just so fast. And afterward, I just feel awful about myself. Like I’ve wasted all this food I meant to share with my friends. I sit there looking at the empty boxes and I just feel so ashamed. I mean, I'm forty-eight years old, I am way too old to be acting this way. I always just sit there feeling terrible, promising myself it won’t ever happen again.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating or control what you're eating during these episodes?

Yes, that's exactly it. What really scares me is that once I start eating... especially when I'm just alone in the kitchen... it feels like I've stepped aside and I can't make myself stop. Even though I'm telling myself the whole time, "Janet, put it away." 

My kitchen is really nice, too. My husband and I remodeled it about five years ago. We put in those beautiful quartz countertops, the ones that look like marble but don't stain when you spill red wine on them. My sister spilled half a glass of merlot on my old Formica counters on Thanksgiving in 2018, and I swear that pink stain never came out. We scrubbed it with baking soda, white vinegar, everything. My grandmother used to swear by white vinegar for cleaning. She used to clean the windows with vinegar and old newspapers. Have you ever tried that? It really does leave them streak-free. Although, getting your hands covered in newsprint ink is such a hassle. You have to wash your hands three times just to get the black smudges off. 

But, um... yes, the eating. It's like I have no control at all once I start. I just keep going until it's gone, no matter how much I tell myself to stop.
Do you usually eat like this when you're feeling stressed, anxious, or upset?

Stress? Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think so. It's not like I have a terrible day and then run to the pantry, if that's what you mean. Sometimes I'm perfectly fine, just having a normal afternoon, and it still happens. Like yesterday, I was just sorting through the mail. We get so much junk mail these days, it's unbelievable. Dozens of catalogs for things I've never even looked at. There's this one company that keeps sending me these thick, glossy catalogs for high-end gardening tools. I don't even have a garden! Well, I have a few potted geraniums on the back patio, but I certainly don't need a hundred-dollar hand-forged trowel from England to take care of them. 

My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, now he has a garden. He grows the most enormous zucchini you've ever seen. He's always leaving them on our porch in the summer because he can't possibly eat them all. Last year, I tried making zucchini bread, but I think I left it in the oven too long because it came out dry as a bone. I used a recipe I found on Pinterest, but honestly, I think those online recipes leave out steps on purpose. Nothing ever turns out like the pictures. 

But anyway... no, it's not really about being upset or anxious. It just sort of... happens. I could be having a perfectly fine day and I still end up eating like that.
Do you consider these episodes of uncontrollable eating to be binge eating episodes?

Binge eating? I... I guess so. I mean, I don't really know what the official word for it is. I just know it's a lot of food and I can't stop. I always thought "binge" was a word people used for watching television. Like my niece, Sarah, she's always talking about binge-watching shows on Netflix. She's in college now, studying communications, whatever that means. When I was her age, people studied things like nursing or teaching. My sister, her mother, is a dental hygienist. She’s worked at the same office for twenty-two years. Dr. Miller’s office over on Elm Street. He's a very nice man, but he always gives out those terrible little travel toothbrushes at the end of your appointment. You know the ones? The bristles are so hard they practically scrape your gums off. I always end up throwing them right in the trash, which feels wasteful, but what else are you supposed to do with them? I tried using one to clean the grout in the master bathroom once, but the handle snapped right in half. 

But um... what were you asking? Oh, right. Yeah, I suppose you could call it binge eating. I don't know the medical terms, I just know I eat way too much and I can't seem to stop myself when it happens.

My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, now he has a garden. He grows the most enormous zucchini you've ever seen. He's always leaving them on our porch in the summer because he can't possibly eat them all. Last year, I tried making zucchini bread, but I think I left it in the oven too long because it came out dry as a bone. I used a recipe I found on Pinterest, but honestly, I think those online recipes leave out steps on purpose. Nothing ever turns out like the pictures. 

But anyway... no, it's not really about being upset or anxious. It just sort of... happens. I could be having a perfectly fine day and I still end up eating like that.

doctor.question: Do you consider these episodes of uncontrollable eating to be binge eating episodes?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient considers these episodes to be 'binge eating episodes', which is asking for a label or self-identification of the behavior rather than a specific symptom criterion like eating a large amount, loss of control, rapid eating, etc. There is no specific symptom profile item for simply agreeing to the term 'binge eating.'

patient.answer:
Binge eating? I... I guess so. I mean, I don't really know what the official word for it is. I just know it's a lot of food and I can't stop. She’s worked at the same office for twenty-two years. Dr. Miller’s office over on Elm Street. He's a very nice man, but he always gives out those terrible little travel toothbrushes at the end of your appointment. You know the ones? I tried using one to clean the grout in the master bathroom once, but the handle snapped right in half. 

But um... what were you asking? Oh, right. Yeah, I suppose you could call it binge eating. I don't know the medical terms, I just know I eat way too much and I can't seem to stop myself when it happens.
